verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 47.14
verses.english: Linked Discourses 47.14

verses.pali: 2. Nālandavagga
verses.english: 2. At Nāḷandā

verses.pali: Ukkacelasutta
verses.english: At Ukkacelā

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vajjīsu viharati ukkacelāyaṁ gaṅgāya nadiyā tīre mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ aciraparinibbutesu sāriputtamoggallānesu.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Vajjis near Ukkacelā on the bank of the Ganges river, together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants. It was not long after Sāriputta and Moggallāna had become fully quenched.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto ajjhokāse nisinno hoti.
verses.english: Now, at that time the Buddha was sitting in the open, surrounded by the Saṅgha of mendicants.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā tuṇhībhūtaṁ bhikkhusaṅghaṁ anuviloketvā bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: Then the Buddha looked around the Saṅgha of mendicants, who were silent. He addressed them:

verses.pali: “api myāyaṁ, bhikkhave, parisā suññā viya khāyati parinibbutesu sāriputtamoggallānesu.
verses.english: “Mendicants, this assembly seems empty to me now that Sāriputta and Moggallāna have become fully quenched.

verses.pali: Asuññā me, bhikkhave, parisā hoti, anapekkhā tassaṁ disāyaṁ hoti, yassaṁ disāyaṁ sāriputtamoggallānā viharanti.
verses.english: My assembly never used to be empty; I had no concern for any region where Sāriputta and Moggallāna stayed.

verses.pali: Ye hi te, bhikkhave, ahesuṁ atītamaddhānaṁ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tesampi bhagavantānaṁ etapparamaṁyeva sāvakayugaṁ ahosi—
verses.english: The Buddhas of the past or the future have pairs of chief disciples who at best were like

verses.pali: seyyathāpi mayhaṁ sāriputtamoggallānā.
verses.english: Sāriputta and Moggallāna were to me.

verses.pali: Yepi te, bhikkhave, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṁ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tesampi bhagavantānaṁ etapparamaṁyeva sāvakayugaṁ bhavissati—seyyathāpi mayhaṁ sāriputtamoggallānā.
Acchariyaṁ, bhikkhave, sāvakānaṁ, abbhutaṁ, bhikkhave, sāvakānaṁ.
verses.english: It’s an incredible and amazing quality of such disciples

verses.pali: Satthu ca nāma sāsanakarā bhavissanti ovādappaṭikarā, catunnañca parisānaṁ piyā bhavissanti manāpā garubhāvanīyā ca.
verses.english: that they fulfill the Teacher’s instructions and follow his advice. And they’re liked and approved, respected and admired by the four assemblies.

verses.pali: Acchariyaṁ, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa, abbhutaṁ, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa.
verses.english: And it’s an incredible and amazing quality of the Realized One

verses.pali: Evarūpepi nāma sāvakayuge parinibbute natthi tathāgatassa soko vā paridevo vā.
verses.english: that when such a pair of disciples becomes fully quenched he does not sorrow or lament.

verses.pali: Taṁ kutettha, bhikkhave, labbhā. Yaṁ taṁ jātaṁ bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ palokadhammaṁ, taṁ vata mā palujjīti—
verses.english: How could it possibly be so that what is born, created, conditioned, and liable to wear out should not wear out?

verses.pali: netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
verses.english: That is not possible.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahato rukkhassa tiṭṭhato sāravato ye mahantatarā khandhā te palujjeyyuṁ;
verses.english: Suppose there was a large tree standing with heartwood, and the largest branches broke off.

verses.pali: evameva kho, bhikkhave, mahato bhikkhusaṅghassa tiṭṭhato sāravato sāriputtamoggallānā parinibbutā.
verses.english: In the same way, in the great Saṅgha that stands with heartwood, Sāriputta and Moggallāna have become fully quenched.

verses.pali: Taṁ kutettha, bhikkhave, labbhā. Yaṁ taṁ jātaṁ bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ palokadhammaṁ, taṁ vata mā palujjīti—
verses.english: How could it possibly be so that what is born, created, conditioned, and liable to wear out should not wear out?

verses.pali: netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
verses.english: That is not possible.

verses.pali: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, attadīpā viharatha attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā.
verses.english: So mendicants, live as your own island, your own refuge, with no other refuge. Let the teaching be your island and your refuge, with no other refuge.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo?
verses.english: And how does a mendicant do this?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: vedanāsu …pe…
verses.english: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

verses.pali: citte …pe…
verses.english: mind …

verses.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant lives as their own island, their own refuge, with no other refuge. That’s how the teaching is their island and their refuge, with no other refuge.

verses.pali: Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, etarahi vā mamaccaye vā attadīpā viharissanti attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā; tamatagge mete, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhavissanti ye keci sikkhākāmā”ti.
verses.english: Whether now or after I have passed, any who shall live as their own island, their own refuge, with no other refuge; with the teaching as their island and their refuge, with no other refuge—those mendicants of mine who want to train shall be among the best of the best.”

verses.pali: Catutthaṁ.
